name: Seahawks Nickel Defense
subtitle: Seattle Seahawks · Madden 27
tagline: Show them two. Send them four.

about.headline: WHO ARE THE SEAHAWKS
copy: Mike Macdonald came to Seattle in 2024 from Baltimore, where his 2023 Ravens defense had led the league in points allowed, sacks and takeaways. By his second season in Seattle the defense was the {ppg|best in the league}, first in scoring at 17.2 points a game and first in DVOA.

They did it in two high shells with big nickel on the field, blitzing less than almost anybody and confusing protections instead: linebackers mugged in the A gaps, tackles dropping into coverage, the nickel coming free off the edge.

Then they won Super Bowl LX {sb|29 to 13} over the Patriots with six sacks, two interceptions and a pick six, holding New England to 78 yards through three quarters. That is the defense we are building, out of the Arizona Cardinals playbook in Madden 27.

principles.title: STOP THE RUN ON EARLY DOWNS
principles.blurb: Win early downs, get them into obvious passing situations, then unleash the rest of the playbook.
principles.detail: Win early downs and the offense is in known passing situations, which is where every sim pressure and every zero in this package lives. The base calls stop the run from two high because the safeties are in the run fit, so the shell never changes and the box still gets loaded.

pages.title: Win early downs, own third down
pages.text: On early downs we are trying to accomplish one thing: get the offense into obvious passing situations. That means stopping the run, controlling the line of scrimmage and limiting the plays down the field, so the most they get is a short gain underneath. Do that on first and second down and it is second and long and third and long, and that is when we start to unleash the rest of the playbook: the sim pressures, the zeros, the disguises.
points: Stop the run and control the line of scrimmage
Keep everything in front: short gains underneath, nothing over the top
Get them into obvious passing downs, then unleash the rest of the playbook

pages.title: Two high, and still nine in the fit
pages.text: Seattle stays in two high shells and still stops the run, because the safeties are in the run fit. Out of Quarters they key number two and come downhill on the handoff, Pounder keeps that fit with man under it, and Show SS Sim 2 walks a safety down to the strength to set the edge and spill the toss. The box gets loaded without the shell ever changing before the snap.
points: The Quarters safeties fit the run because they read the slot, not the quarterback
The walked down safety on Show SS Sim 2 always goes to the strength
The number one scoring defense in the league did it from two high

pages.title: Quarters, Palms, Show SS Sim 2, Pounder
pages.text: First and ten you are in Quarters against two by two or Palms against three by one, with one safety usered and roving. When you want the box loaded, Show SS Sim 2, flipped to the side with more bodies, so the safety sets the edge and still comes as a four man sim on the pass. Pounder is the man version with both safeties fitting. Silver Shoot Pinch works on first down too, because everybody is flying to the football.
points: Flip Show SS Sim 2 to the two tight end side, the bunch side, the wing side
User a safety in Pounder and play him with quarters rules
Second and long is where the sim pressures start

principles.title: CONFUSE THE PROTECTION
principles.blurb: Threaten six, rush four. The protection slides to a blitz that never comes and one of ours walks in free.
principles.detail: Threaten six and send four. The mugged linebackers and the walked up nickel make the protection slide, and then the ones they blocked for drop out while the nickel comes free. Seattle blitzed less than almost anybody in the league and still got home, because the front moves and the center never knows which four are coming.

pages.title: Make the protection wrong before the snap
pages.text: A sim pressure shows a blitz and rushes four. The mugged linebackers and the walked up nickel force the line to slide and the back to stay in, and then the players they protected against drop into coverage. The rusher who comes free was never the one they were worried about. Four on the quarterback, seven in coverage, and the ball has to come out before anybody is open.
points: The protection has to account for everybody who could come
Whoever the line slides toward is the one who drops
Seven in coverage against three or four in routes is the math we want every snap

pages.title: Bottom of the league in blitzes, top in stunts
pages.text: Seattle blitzed less than almost anybody in 2025, about a fifth of the snaps, and ranked near the top of the league in stunts and games up front. Macdonald says himself they do not run that many sim pressures. The pressure comes from the front moving: linebackers in the A gaps, tackles dropping into the hook, the nickel off the edge, so the center never knows which four are coming.
points: A 21.8 percent blitz rate, fifth in the league in stunt usage
A defensive tackle in the passing lane is the look nobody prepares for
Number one in DVOA rushing four most of the time

pages.title: Nickel Sim 2, SS Dog 3, SS Sim 2, Redzone DT Drop
pages.text: The user is the lie. Hover half a second in the gap so the tackle bites, then get out, and the nickel comes unblocked off the edge. Nickel Sim 2 slides and crashes the line to him, SS Dog 3 and SS Sim 2 do it out of the double mug with a tackle dropping, and Redzone DT Drop drops both tackles under the hot routes with man behind it.
points: Hover, make the tackle bite, get out
Cover 3 behind Nickel Sim 2 and SS Dog 3, Cover 2 invert behind SS Sim 2
When they keep the back in, it is seven on four on the back end

principles.title: CREATE THE BIG PLAY
principles.blurb: Sacks, takeaways and touchdowns. This defense is built to end drives, not just get off the field.
principles.detail: Unblocked heat makes the quarterback throw early into a coverage with more defenders than receivers, and that is where the picks come from. The zeros get the sacks, the sims get the panicked throws, and the match coverage behind both is already sitting in the window.

pages.title: Pressure plus numbers equals takeaways
pages.text: Unblocked heat makes the quarterback throw early and off his back foot, into a coverage with more defenders than receivers. That is where the interceptions come from. The zero pressures get the sacks, the sim pressures force the panicked throw, and the match coverage behind both is already sitting in the window when it comes.
points: Every pick on the film came off a throw made under pressure
A seam flat matching number two is already in the window
The zero is the sack call, the sim is the takeaway call

pages.title: Six sacks and a pick six in the Super Bowl
pages.text: The 2025 Seahawks were the number one scoring defense at 17.2 points a game and the number one defense in DVOA, sixth best in DVOA history. In Super Bowl LX they sacked the Patriots six times, picked them twice, took one back for a touchdown, and held them to 78 yards through three quarters in a 29 to 13 win. Leonard Williams had a 92 yard pick six of his own during the season.
points: 17.2 points a game, first in the league
Six sacks, two picks, a pick six and a forced fumble in the Super Bowl
Witherspoon, Williams and Ernest Jones all second team All Pro

pages.title: Silver Shoot Pinch, LB Pop 0, Blitz Loop 3, LB Blitz 6
pages.text: When it has to come in, Blitz Loop 3 brings five over three blockers and the nickel is free every time. Silver Shoot Pinch and LB Pop 0 are the zeros: two free rushers and the ball out in half a second. LB Blitz 6 is the five man pressure with match coverage behind it, so when it gets picked up the user is sitting in the middle for the quick throw.
points: Read deep to short as the user and let the flat defenders take the throws over their heads
Seam flats on for long yardage, hard flats on short yardage
The user has the back on every zero

playbook.title: RUN THE CARDINALS PLAYBOOK
playbook.note: In Madden 27 this whole defense runs out of the ARIZONA CARDINALS playbook. All three Seahawks installs do, so every call mixes and matches into one scheme.

jobs: MEG ON NUMBER ONE IN PALMS, MAN EVERYWHERE HE GOES.
MAN ON DEMAND IN QUARTERS: VERTICAL, LOCK HIM UP.
PRESS ON THE ISLAND WHEN THE SAFETIES PINCH INSIDE.
JUMP THE OUT BY NUMBER TWO ON THE TWO READ.
COME FREE OFF THE EDGE ON EVERY SIM PRESSURE.
MATCH NUMBER TWO VERTICAL IN THE SEAM FLAT.
ERASE THE CHECKDOWN IN THE HARD FLAT.
LOCK THE SLOT ON POUNDER AND THE ZEROS.
EAT THE DOUBLE TEAM ON EARLY DOWNS.
SLANT TO THE BLITZ SIDE ON THE PRESSURES.
DROP INTO THE HOOK ON REDZONE DT DROP AND SS DOG 3.
GET THE SHED WHEN THEY BLOCK THE BACK.
MUG THE A GAP AND MAKE THE CENTER SLIDE.
HOVER HALF A SECOND, THEN GET OUT.
STEP IN FRONT OF THE QUICK THROW OVER THE MIDDLE.
COME FREE ON THE ZEROS.
SET THE EDGE AGAINST THE TOSS.
SLANT DOWN SO THE NICKEL COMES FREE OUTSIDE.
CONTAIN THE QUARTERBACK WHEN CONTAIN IS ON.
DROP AND PLAY THE MIDDLE AS THE BACKSIDE END.
SHOW TWO HIGH ON EVERY SNAP.
WALK DOWN TO THE STRENGTH ON SHOW SS SIM 2.
FIT THE RUN OUT OF QUARTERS AND POUNDER.
READ DEEP TO SHORT AS THE USER.

plays.name: Cover 4 Quarters

reads.label: Quarters Against Two by Two
reads.text: Rotate through Quarters and Palms as the base. Quarters is the call against two by two, even sets: both corners take an outside quarter, both safeties an inside quarter and read number two, and the nickel and the linebackers match underneath. The full rules are on the site and in the two college deep dives, and they are the same in Madden.

reads.label: User a Safety and Rove
reads.text: Always user one of the two safeties. Once the match rules have everybody else accounted for, you are basically free, roving and helping on anything you see: the deep crosser comes across, you take it, and the other safety steps down to disrupt the throw into his window.

reads.label: All Nine in the Run Fit
reads.text: The front four, the nickel, both linebackers and both safeties are all in run fits out of Nickel 2-4. As soon as they see run, everybody fires downhill: safeties fire, linebackers fire, ends fire. It is just a great run defense.

reads.label: Everything Boxed, Four Rushing
reads.text: Double team deep, boxed, boxed, and still a four man pressure with the front four. He tries to throw it on the run and there are two of ours at the catch point. That freedom on the back end is why match is the base.

reads.label: Against Bunch, the Box Check
reads.text: Quarters against bunch is the Box check, on the Cover 4 checks sheet. Later Seahawks installs go deeper on bunch and the other odd sets.

adjustments: No setup needed
User one of the two safeties
Rotate it with Palms: Quarters against two by two, Palms against three by one
Against bunch: the Box check
plays.whenToUse: One of the base calls in almost every scheme, because it is the most adaptable way to play defense in Madden and college football. It stops the run with all nine in the fit, it plays the pass with match rules, and once you understand how it works the user has almost free rein to make plays on the back end. Call it against two by two.

rules.title: Cover 4 Quarters
rules.intro: These are the rules for match coverage, not a formation. They travel: any scheme, any front you are lined up in can play them, and the numbering never changes.

shots.t: Quarters vs bunch, the box check
shots.img: art/Bama Assets__Quarters Vs Bunch Screen Shot.webp

b: #1 is the outside receiver.
#2 is the next man in, slot or tight end.
#3 only shows up on trips.
Reads run outside in.

sections.t: The corner: MOD, man on demand, reads #1 to #2
b: #1 goes vertical (five yards or more) and he locks him up in man.
#1 breaks in or shallow and he zones off, looking to help on #2. If #2 runs a corner or a streak he doubles him.
Both stay short and he sinks back into the deep quarter.
#2 goes vertical and the safety plays him man. Streaks, corners, posts.
#2 breaks in or shallow and he scans to #1 to bracket anything deep.
Both stay shallow and he is free help over the middle, doubling crossers from the other side.

sections.t: The quarter flat: nickel or apex
b: Cap #2 if he releases vertical, then get eyes to the flat and take anything out there.
#2 goes flat right away and he covers him.
#2 runs a wheel and he matches it upfield, converting to man.
No flat threat and he buzzes under any dig or curl behind him.
On a drag: away from the back he carries it across. On the back's side he passes it to the three receiver hook.

sections.t: The three receiver hook: the free man
b: In 2x2 he is mostly free, with no locked in man assignment.
His job is to help over the middle and pick up crossers or late flat routes.
He takes the second player to the flat: once the quarter flat gets run off, the next one out there is his.
A floater. He doubles crossers, jumps underneath routes and cleans up the space the quarter flat cannot reach.
Corners, crossers, deep posts. Quarters takes every one of them away.
The corners play man on demand, so nothing gets in behind them.
The safeties read and close on anything vertical.
Double teams sit at the catch point, out of a two high shell that tells the offense nothing.
Still match coverage, not a spot drop. Matched by quadrant, not by receiver number.
Corner takes the first one deep and outside, safety the first one deep and inside.
Quarter flat takes the first one shallow and outside, three receiver hook the first one shallow and inside.
Nobody starts with a man. Everybody starts with a direction.
Backside: the corner plays man everywhere on the solo receiver, the backside quarter flat mans up the back if he releases, and the backside safety is the one you user, free to help on anybody.
The exact same box check with one change: the corner locks onto #1 in man if he stays outside, instead of reading his quadrant.
Tested against every variation of flood and it holds. This is the adjustment to use against bunch.

reads.label: Palms Against Three by One
reads.text: The other half of the rotation. Palms is the call against three by one: the same two high shell as Quarters, the same numbering, with the corner and the safety reading number two together. The full rules are on the site and in the two college deep dives, and they are the same in Madden.

reads.label: User the Weak Side Safety
reads.text: Against three by one, user the weak side safety, because now you are basically free, roving and looking to help on anything you see. Against bunch, user the solo side safety: bunch gets matched all across the field and you are free over the middle when the backside number one breaks in.

reads.label: Empty and the Out and Up
reads.text: Palms against empty too. Double team deep, the out and up gets matched across the field, and there is nowhere to go. He throws the deep corner route, Nick Emmanwori is step for step, click on and high point it for the pick.

reads.label: The Same Run Fit
reads.text: The same nine in the fit as Quarters: safeties fire, linebackers fire, ends fire. String the run out and gang tackle it.

reads.label: The Checks
reads.text: Palms against bunch is Bingo, against trips it is Stump, and against a one receiver side with a tight end it is Solo Cut. They are all on the Cover 4 checks sheet.

adjustments: No setup needed
Against three by one, user the weak side safety and rove
Against bunch, user the solo side safety
Rotate it with Quarters: Palms against three by one and empty
Checks: bunch is Bingo, trips is Stump, one receiver tight is Solo Cut
plays.whenToUse: The base call against three by one, and against empty as well. Rotate it with Quarters so the picture stays the same and the rules change, and use the free safety to make plays on the back end. Later Seahawks installs go deeper on bunch and the other odd sets.

rules.title: Cover 4 Palms
rules.intro: Palms is the trips call. The same two high shell as Quarters, the same numbering, and the corner and the safety read together so the flat gets jumped and the deep stuff gets doubled. Against empty it is two sets of rules in one call.

shots.img: art/Bama Assets__Palms Vs Trips Screen Shot.webp
art/Bama Assets__Palms Vs Empty Screen Shot.webp

b: #1 is always the outside receiver.
#2 is the next man in, slot or tight end.
#3 is the inside most man in the trips.
Everything counts outside in.

sections.t: The trips corner: MEG, man everywhere he goes
b: MEG on #1. Man everywhere he goes, no exceptions.
Vertical, inside, across the field, it does not matter. He travels.
No switching and no passing off. This is pure man.

sections.t: The nickel or apex on the trips side: reads #3 to #2
b: #3 goes fast to the flat (arrow, whip, quick out) and he takes him right away, matching him to the flat and running with him.
#3 goes vertical or into the middle (five yards or more, seam or crosser) and he snaps his eyes to #2 and mans him up.
Once he is on #2 he takes him anywhere on the field, short or deep.
#3 goes vertical and the safety takes him. Seam, post, corner, anything vertical.
#3 stays shallow and #2 goes vertical and he picks up #2 and takes him wherever he goes.
Both #2 and #3 stay shallow and he is free help over the top, usually doubling #1 on a post or a deep dig.
First rule: wall off #3 if he goes vertical or crosses. Stay underneath him until the safety takes it, then drift back into space.
If the back is already taken by the apex and somebody else comes into that flat late, the Mike picks him up.
Otherwise he sits in the middle, reads the quarterback and looks for crossers and digs.

sections.t: The solo apex: quarter flat, man on the back
b: He has the running back. Swing, angle or wheel, it is man everywhere he goes.
If the back stays in to block he sits in the flat, watches for late releases and drives on checkdowns.

sections.t: The solo safety: the robber, your user
b: This is the free player. He is your robber and he can help anywhere.
#1 on his side goes vertical and he brackets him with the corner.
#1 breaks inside or shallow and he looks back across the field to help on crossers from the trips side.
That back side help on crossers and deep digs is what makes Palms elite.
MEG on #1. Man everywhere he goes.
If the solo side is an inline tight end instead of a receiver: vertical or a corner route and he takes him man.
If that tight end breaks inside, the safety takes him across and this corner looks for work from the trips side.

sections.t: Against empty: two sets of rules, one call
b: Empty is just 3x2. The trips side plays straight Palms, counting 3 to 2. The two receiver side plays Palms against 2x2 and traps the flat.
Nobody is holding a back, so everybody is on a receiver.
The two receiver side corner sits on #2 to the flat instead of bailing. That is the trap: quick outs and flat routes get jumped, and the safety takes #1 over the top the second the corner drives.
#2 and #1 both vertical and both defenders lock on in man. #2 runs a wheel and the corner carries him and converts to man.
If one side has an inline tight end instead of a true slot, that side plays standard Quarters: corner in MOD on #1, safety reading #2 to #1, apex jamming #2 and taking the first man to the flat.
Takes away the corner routes and flood concepts trips lives on.
You still get a free robber on the back side.
Two high shell, so it gives up nothing pre snap.
Still fits the run with the safeties.

plays.name: Show SS Sim 2

reads.label: Stop the Run and Play the Pass
reads.text: A base call has to do both. The strong safety walks down and gives us a loaded box on the run, and on the pass he fires off the edge as a four man sim pressure with everybody else dropping out. Super balanced, so it can be called on any down.

reads.label: Only Four Rushing
reads.text: One, two, three, four. The safety comes unblocked off the edge and he is there by the time the quarterback hits the back of his drop. Even when they block it up, which they will sometimes, we are still dropping everybody else into coverage.

reads.label: The Deep Cloud Flats
reads.text: The corners sit in deep cloud flats, so when he tries to throw it up over our heads the safety and the corner meet at the football.

reads.label: The User Over the Middle
reads.text: You are in the mid read, sitting in the gap between the end and the tackle on the blitz side. Anything over the middle, step in front of it. Ernest Jones took one back for six on fourth and seven.

reads.label: The Run Fit
reads.text: The walked down safety is on the strength, so when they run the toss to the bunch side he holds the edge, the end scrapes over the top and the corners flow down. It shuts down outside runs, and it gets good sheds inside when they run it up the middle.

adjustments: When you break the huddle the strong safety often walks down on the weak side: flip the play so he is on the strength, the two tight end side, the bunch side, the wing side, whichever side has more players
Against a two by two set with no strong side, you do not have to flip it
Shift the D-line to the side the safety walked down on
QB contain
User the linebacker in the mid read and stay down in the gap between the end and the tackle on that side
plays.whenToUse: A base call you can make at any time in the game: first and ten, second and ten, even fourth and seven. It does both jobs, the walked down safety loads the box and holds the edge against the run, and on the pass it is a four man sim pressure with unblocked heat and everybody else in coverage.

plays.name: Silver Shoot Pinch

reads.label: Two Free Rushers
reads.text: If they send everybody out, the looping linebacker comes up the middle and the nickel comes off the edge, and both get there. Super fast pressure. Against play action it was four free rushers in on Mahomes.

reads.label: The Back Decides Who Is Free
reads.text: If the back stays in, he usually blocks the looper and the nickel is free. If he shoots out to the nickel, the looper is free. Either way the ball has to be out right now.

reads.label: You Have Whoever Is Uncovered
reads.text: Man across the board, and the user has the running back or the tight end, whoever nobody is locked on. Back goes out on a swing, run out with him. Back stays in, you are free to help over the middle on the tight end or the post.

reads.label: A Run Defense Too
reads.text: With everybody flying to the football this holds up against the run. Not the best run defense in the package, but it is a first and ten call when you have no idea what they are running.

adjustments: Slant the D-line to the side the nickel is blitzing from
Blitz all linebackers
User the linebacker on the same side as the nickel
Do not blitz him: walk him down one or two steps into the gap between the tackles
You have the back or whoever is uncovered in man
plays.whenToUse: The zero pressure with two free rushers when they send everybody out, and super fast pressure when they do not. With everybody flying to the football it works like a base call too, so you can call it on first and ten when you are not sure what they are running.

plays.name: LB Blitz 6

reads.label: Blitzing With Match Coverage
reads.text: A Cover 6 shell on the back end behind a five man pressure. We are relying on the heat to get there, and if they keep extra guys in to block, the coverage is good enough to hold.

reads.label: Look to the Cover 2 Side First
reads.text: The three players on the quarters side do a really good job matching two or three receivers, so as the user open up to the Cover 2 side first. Nothing there, shoot your eyes back to the quarters side.

reads.label: Unblocked off the Edge
reads.text: When they send everybody out, the pressure comes unblocked on the side away from the user. Hover for half a second and get out over the middle.

reads.label: When It Gets Blocked Up
reads.text: They block the back and it gets picked up. Fine. Now you are in the middle of the field looking for who is not getting matched. He tries the quick throw over the middle and a match defender steps right in front of it.

adjustments: Shift the D-line away from the side the two walked down linebackers are on
Slant the D-line out
Blitz all linebackers
User the outside one of the two walked down linebackers
If it is not coming in, try QB contain with the same setup
plays.whenToUse: The blitz that keeps match coverage behind it. It does not come in every single time, but it is only a five man pressure with such good coverage on the back end that it is really effective, and a picked up blitz does not turn into a big play.

plays.name: SS Dog 3

reads.label: Four Rushing, Seven Dropping
reads.text: The user hovers for half a second so the tackle has to respect him and bite inside, then gets out. That is what lets the nickel come unblocked off the edge. One, two, three, four rushing, seven dropping out, unblocked pressure as he hits the back of his drop.

reads.label: The Three Receiver Hook Is a Tackle
reads.text: It is not just linebackers dropping in this defense. A defensive tackle drops out into the three receiver hook here. Byron Murphy saw the drag coming across and stepped in front for the pick on fourth and eight.

reads.label: The Seam Flats Match
reads.text: The seam flats match verticals from number two. With you and the three receiver hook in the middle, you play over the middle unless number two goes to the flat, and if your seam flat gets run off, go help in the flat. Witherspoon stepped in front of one for a huge pick.

reads.label: They Block the Back
reads.text: If they keep the back in, they can block it up. Fine, because we can still get sheds, and now it is seven on four on the back end. Shade down to hard flats and the quick throws to the flat get wiped out: Witherspoon took one for six.

adjustments: QB contain right away
User the linebacker on the same side as the blitzing nickel
Do not blitz him: hover for half a second so the tackle bites inside, then get out
Seam flats stay on; shade down to hard flats to take away the quick throws to the flat
plays.whenToUse: A sim pressure, the kind Mike Macdonald runs a lot of: four rush, seven drop, and unblocked heat off the edge once the tackle bites inside. Any time you want pressure without giving up the numbers on the back end.

plays.name: Redzone DT Drop

reads.label: Four Rush, Unblocked Edge
reads.text: One, two, three, four come and the nickel comes free off the edge basically every time they send everybody out. Even when they block the back, six on four, the nickel still comes unblocked.

reads.label: The Tackles Drop Out
reads.text: Both defensive tackles drop into hook curls under the quick hitters, which is the weirdest look for people to attack. Byron Murphy under a post for the knockdown, Leonard Williams at six foot six skying up to swat one.

reads.label: Man Across the Board
reads.text: Man coverage everywhere behind it, so you need guys who hold up one on one and make plays on the ball. The tackles take the hot routes over the middle that man usually gives up.

reads.label: You Have Whoever Is Uncovered
reads.text: As the user you have whoever is uncovered in man. A lot of the time that is the running back out of trips or bunch, sometimes a slot or a tight end. Know who it is before the snap.

adjustments: QB contain
User the outside one of the two linebackers on the line, beside the defensive end
Hover and get out; you have whoever is uncovered in man
plays.whenToUse: Incredibly easy to set up and a totally different wrinkle: a four man sim with man across the board and both tackles dropping out under the quick hitters. Really good pressure, and a look people do not know how to attack.

plays.name: Nickel Sim 2

reads.label: Unblocked Nickel off the Edge
reads.text: The whole point of a sim pressure: we get home with four. Slide the line to the nickel and crash it down, and the nickel comes free off the edge while the backside end drops out. Hit before he can hit the back of his drop.

reads.label: Only Four Rushing
reads.text: One, two, three, four. The user on the backside is free to play over the middle, so it is three defenders in the middle of the field plus the deep shell. The numbers advantage in the secondary is massive.

reads.label: When They Block the Back
reads.text: Block the back and it is six blocking four. Sometimes that blocks it up, and sometimes it still comes in. Because we outnumber them so badly on the blitz side, sometimes the end shoots out and the nickel loops inside. Max protect it and they only have three out on routes against our seven.

reads.label: Off Coverage on Long Yardage
reads.text: Third and twenty seven, fourth and thirteen: our guys are playing off, seven dropping into coverage. He throws it up and the flat defender steps in front for the pick.

adjustments: Slide the D-line to the blitzing nickel
Crash the D-line down
User the backside defensive end, away from the blitz
Cloud flats stay on the field, shade down to hard flats if you want
plays.whenToUse: A really easy setup and an unblocked nickel off the edge while rushing only four. Second and long, third and long, fourth and long, any time you want pressure without taking anyone out of coverage.

plays.name: 2 Invert Lurk

reads.label: Looks Like Cover 2, Then Inverts
reads.text: Pre snap it is just normal Cover 2. Once the ball is snapped we invert it: the safety comes down and plays more like a robber in the seam in the middle of the field, and the picture changes on him. Keep the user safety back so it shows two high until the snap.

reads.label: Read Deep to Short
reads.text: You are the high safety in the hook curl. Is anything taking me deep? No. Now get aggressive and help anywhere. Anything attacking the seam, sit right on it, because you are already at depth like another deep defender.

reads.label: Play the Sticks on Fourth and Long
reads.text: Coverage, then Play the Sticks. Now the flat defenders play at sixteen yards and nothing gets over their heads. A corner route at the sticks got skied and picked on fourth and sixteen.

reads.label: Run to Your Side
reads.text: Because you are the safety, a run to your side lets you fly downhill and get super aggressive. Three yard loss on an outside toss.

adjustments: No setup, it looks like normal Cover 2
User the high safety in the hook curl and keep him back so it shows two high
Shade up or down as you like
Fourth and long: Coverage, then Play the Sticks
plays.whenToUse: The safe coverage with a disguise built in. Mix it in with the match coverages and the blitzes as one more look, and lean on it when you just want to play a nice safe shell and read deep to short.

plays.name: Pounder

reads.label: Man Under, Quarters Over the Top
reads.text: Treat it like Cover 2 Man with the two high safeties playing quarters. In the game files those two are supposed to play match, but a lot of the time they play more like drop zone, so user one of them and play him with quarters rules yourself.

reads.label: The Middle of the Field
reads.text: In Cover 2 Man the safeties get pulled outside in deep halves to help on the outside players. Here they focus on the middle of the field, the tight end and the slot receivers, where people want to throw the ball anyway.

reads.label: Get Aggressive With the User
reads.text: Play action, and the user safety comes down on it. Then it is the deep crosser: get out underneath it and take it away, while the non user safety caps the vertical routes from the interior, even out of bunch. We stepped in front for a knockout at the catch point on fourth and twenty three.

reads.label: Still Rushing Four
reads.text: It is a very good coverage defense, but we are not dropping everybody out. The front four still get home, so he does not have all day to hold it against the man coverage.

reads.label: Both Safeties in the Run Fit
reads.text: Because the safeties are in quarters they are in run fits, which they are not in Cover 2 Man. So it is two man under with much better run defense. Fire into the ball with the safety and hold it to two.

adjustments: User one of the high safeties and play him with quarters rules
On play action come down with him, then get under the crosser
plays.whenToUse: Man coverage underneath with the safeties taking away the middle of the field, and both of them still in the run fit. It is basically quarters run defense while playing man, so it works against the run and the pass.

plays.name: SS Sim 2

reads.label: Four Rushers, Pressure off the Edge
reads.text: One, two, three, four. Only four rushing, and two came free before he could even hit the back of his drop off play action. It still lets us drop everybody else out.

reads.label: A Different Look Behind It
reads.text: Instead of the Cover 3 behind Nickel Sim 2 and SS Dog 3, this is a Cover 2 invert with match principles: a seam flat, a mid read and a cloud flat. Same pressure, a different picture for the quarterback.

reads.label: Look for the Hot
reads.text: When we expect unblocked pressure, the user starts looking for hots. Two guys dropping to one side, you are responsible for the other. See the quick out, jump it, pass break up at the catch point.

reads.label: The Tackle Drops Too
reads.text: The defensive tackle drops into the hook curl on one side while the mid read sits in the middle, so your hot is the other way. On the goal line the tight end came underneath, the linebacker in the mid jumped it, and we picked it right before the half.

adjustments: The safety auto walks down; whatever side he walks down to, shift the D-line to that side
User the linebacker on the same side as the blitzer, stand him over the tackle, and blitz him
Hover just long enough to make the tackle come down inside, then get out
Shade down to hard flats or leave the cloud and the seam on the field
plays.whenToUse: The change up to the Cover 3 sim pressures. The same four man heat off the edge with a really unique shell behind it, a seam flat, a cloud flat, a mid read and a hook curl, so the quarterback who has learned Nickel Sim 2 gets a different picture.

plays.name: LB Pop 0

reads.label: Two Free Rushers
reads.text: A zero man pressure, and the point of every one of these is fast, nasty pressure. Overload the protection so that even when they block extra backs and tight ends, we still get free runners. He barely hits the back of his drop before he goes down.

reads.label: Half a Second
reads.text: If he sends everybody out on one of these, he has to get the football out in half a second. Two free rushers, three on two on one side, somebody comes through every time.

reads.label: You Have the Back
reads.text: As the user you always have whoever is uncovered in man, usually the running back, sometimes a tight end or a slot. Back goes out, go out with him. Back stays in to block, somebody else comes free anyway.

reads.label: Man Across the Board
reads.text: Man coverage everywhere, so the corners have to win. He tried to hit the crosser under the pressure and Josh Jobe undercut it for a pick six, and Julian Love high pointed the deep ball off the boot.

adjustments: Shift the D-line away from the blitzing nickel
Blitz all linebackers
User the linebacker on the blitz side, the same side as the nickel
Hover and get out; you have the back
If it is not coming in, try QB contain to change the angles
plays.whenToUse: One of the zero pressures every scheme needs a few of. Fast, nasty pressure that overloads the protection, so even when they keep extra backs and tight ends in to block we still get free runners. If he sends everybody out, the ball has to be out in half a second.

plays.name: Blitz Loop 3

reads.label: Five on Three
reads.text: The nickel comes free and the looper comes up the middle. It is basically five defenders coming over three blockers, so a lot of the time a second guy sneaks through too. The backside tackle does nothing except sometimes pick up a looper.

reads.label: Not a Sim Pressure
reads.text: Sim pressures are four on five, so sometimes they get blocked up. This is five, and if they do not block the running back it comes in every single time, from the nickel or from the looper up the middle.

reads.label: The Seam Flats Match
reads.text: Leave the seam flats on the field and they match the vertical routes. Fourth and twenty seven, three guys free, he has to push it down the field and there is nothing there. Third and two or fourth and three, shade down to hard flats and take away the quick hitters.

reads.label: You Are the Only Middle Help
reads.text: As the user in the three receiver hook you are the help in the middle of the field. Hover and get out. He tries to go quick up the seam, jump to it and step in front.

adjustments: Shift the D-line to the blitz side
Blitz all linebackers
User the outside one of the two standing linebackers, leave the inside one
Seam flats stay on; on short yardage shade down to hard flats
plays.whenToUse: The pressure for when it has to come in. Five rushers, and if they send everybody out the nickel is unblocked basically every time. Long yardage with the seam flats matching behind it, and hard flats on third and two or fourth and three.
